details.purpose: To record quantitative measurements of specular microscopy.
details.keywords: Cornea, specular microscopy, ECD, Endothelial Cell Density.
details.use:
Use to record the results of corneal specular microscopy, including endothelial cell density, cell size variation, and cell morphology.
The primary use case is monitoring corneal endothelial health before and after intraocular surgery, including glaucoma drainage device surgery, cataract surgery, corneal transplantation, and long-term contact lens wear.
An event time represents the date/time of image acquisition. Multiple events may be recorded to represent serial assessments.
Aligned with the Royal College of Ophthalmologists Glaucoma Procedure Dataset (2024/PROF/483) requirement to record central endothelial cell density.
details.misuse: Do not use for recording full corneal topography or pachymetry results — use a dedicated corneal topography or pachymetry archetype Do not use for recording confocal microscopy results.

items.items: Measurements of corneal endothelial cell quantity, density and morphology obtained by specular microscopy.
Default, unspecified point-in-time event which may be explicitly defined in a template or at run time.
Identification of the eye from which the specular microscopy results were obtained.
The number of corneal endothelial cells per mm², measured in the central cornea by specular microscopy.
The mean area of individual endothelial cells in square micrometres (µm²). Reciprocally related to cell density.
Coefficient of variation (CV) of endothelial cell area, expressed as a percentage. A measure of cell size variability.
Percentage of corneal endothelial cells that are hexagonal (six-sided). A measure of pleomorphism, also called Hexagonality or 6A
Clinical interpretation of the specular microscopy findings for this eye.
Overall clinical interpretation of the specular microscopy examination, combining findings from both eyes where applicable.
Factors that may have affected the quality or reliability of the specular microscopy images, such as poor fixation, corneal oedema, or patient cooperation.
Additional information required to capture local content or to align with other reference models/formalisms.
Additional narrative about the measurement, not captured in other fields.
Number of cells which were recognised an used to calculate the results.
